samples.summary: Divider drag has no `pointercancel` handler — now that `touch-action: none` makes touch dragging actually work, a cancelled touch pointer leaves the drag permanently "in flight"
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:490-514: `onDividerPointerDown` registers `pointermove`/`pointerup` on `window` and only removes them from `onUp` (the `pointerup` handler). Nothing listens for `pointercancel`. The diff's new `divider.style.touchAction = 'none'` is what first makes a finger drag reach this handler, and touch is exactly the input where the browser fires `pointercancel` instead of `pointerup` (second finger / pinch-zoom, system gesture, OS interruption). When that happens: (a) the stale `onMove` stays bound to `window`, so every later `pointermove` — no button held, finger anywhere on the page — keeps recomputing `splitRatio` and rewriting `editorEl.style.flex` / `preview.el.style.flex`, i.e. the split pane follows the pointer forever; (b) `document.body.style.cursor = 'col-resize'` and `userSelect = 'none'` (set at :509-510) are never removed, so text selection stays disabled document-wide; (c) `endDrag` (:508) holds only the *latest* drag's `onUp`, so a subsequent successful drag's `onUp` clears only its own listener and `dispose()` (:629) cannot tear down the orphaned one — the leak survives editor unmount. The same stuck state is reachable with a mouse whose `pointerup` is lost outside the window, since no `setPointerCapture` is used either; the change makes the touch path the newly reachable one.

samples.summary: Share-link image-upload failures are silent: the share-token uploader rejects and `SharedNotesLayout` supplies no catch/toast, unlike the workspace route
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:71-74 hands the engine `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` raw. That uploader (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:40-49`) has no try/catch — `postShareTokenImage` throws on a rejected type, an oversized file, a 403 from a viewer token, or a network error, so the returned promise REJECTS. The notes engine's contract (`packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:16-26`) treats a rejection as "the host already reported this": it drops the placeholder with only a console entry. The workspace route deliberately wraps the same operation (`notes-detail.tsx:208-231`: catch → `toast.error(...)` → return `null`). Net effect for an anonymous editor-role visitor: the "Uploading …" ghost disappears and no image and no error message ever appear, so a failed upload is indistinguishable from a silently lost one.

samples.summary: Widening the divider to 25px amplifies an existing drag-tracking offset: the hairline can now sit ~20px away from the pointer
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:494-498 computes `ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width` and feeds it to the panes' flex-basis percentages, while the divider itself is `flex: 0 0 auto` at a now-25px width (`:284`). The two panes' bases sum to 100% of the container *plus* the divider's 25px, so flex-shrink redistributes: the rendered pane boundary lands at roughly `ratio * (W - 25)` rather than at `ratio * W`. The visible 1px hairline therefore trails the pointer by up to ~21px at the 0.85 clamp (previously ~6px with the 7px divider) — the drag feels detached, and the effect grows exactly in proportion to the width the diff increased.

samples.summary: The divider comment's stated motivation ("a fingernail on a phone") describes a mode that is unreachable below the mobile breakpoint
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:276-294 justifies the 25px hit area and `touch-action` by phone usability, but the divider is only displayed in split mode (`applyViewMode`, :473), and split is filtered out of the view menu below 768px (`notes-toolbar.tsx:404-406`) and demoted to `edit` by both hosts (`notes-detail.tsx:119-120`, `shared-notes-layout.tsx:61-62`). So on a ≤767px viewport the divider never renders; the change only takes effect on touch devices at 768px and up. The behavior is fine — the recorded reason is not the reachable one.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: onDividerPointerDown (editor.ts:490-513) adds only window 'pointermove' (:511) and 'pointerup' (:512); onUp (:500-507) removes only those, and no 'pointercancel' or setPointerCapture/lostpointercapture exists anywhere under packages/notes (repo-wide grep found such handlers only in design-editor, slides, and frontend board/hooks). onMove (:494-499) has no button/pointerId guard, so a pointercancel-terminated touch drag leaves a live window listener that keeps rewriting splitRatio and both flex values, and leaves document.body cursor/user-select (:509-510) unrestored. endDrag is a single slot (:508) so dispose() (:629) cannot tear down an orphaned handler, making the leak survive unmount. The diff's divider.style.touchAction = 'none' (:294, with a comment saying pointermove otherwise never reaches the handler) is what makes the touch path — precisely the input that fires pointercancel — newly reachable. No counterexample found: 'note-divider' occurs only at :274, editor.test.ts has no divider coverage, and packages/frontend/src/app/notes has no cancel/cleanup path. Major: reachable on normal touch use, leaves split pane following the pointer and text selection disabled document-wide.
